Freshness check -- items 1,2,3,4,5,9,12,13,14 are dated Fri Nov 13 (within the last 24-48h); no Saturday-specific breaking news was found beyond continuation of Friday's moves (crypto deleveraging, Middle East posturing) as of Sat ~07:00 SGT, and the Sunday-evening oil/futures reopen has not yet occurred so is not covered here -- re-check Sun evening/Mon Asia open.

items.headline: Nvidia closes below $4T market cap, posts sixth straight weekly decline (-12.75%) -- longest losing streak since 2012
items.summary: Nvidia fell 2.01% on Friday to close below $4T market cap for the first time since July 2025, capping its worst weekly run (-12.75%) in over a decade as the fallout from Jensen Huang's Nov 12 resignation (over alleged affairs including one with a woman flagged by US intelligence as a suspected Chinese asset) continues to weigh on the stock. Analysts estimate Huang's exit could cost Nvidia as much as 20% of its market value given his central role in the AI buildout narrative.
items.actionable: The leadership vacuum at the center of the AI/chip complex is now a confirmed multi-week drawdown (not a one-day shock), and it is the single biggest driver of this week's HK tech and regional risk-off -- keep 0700.HK/1810.HK/0981.HK sized defensively until Nvidia's interim-CEO transition and the Senate chip-export probe (see item below) show signs of stabilizing.

items.headline: Weekend crypto crash: Bitcoin breaks below $70K to ~$67.5K on $1.64B liquidation wave; Ethereum under $2,000
items.summary: Bitcoin sliced through its 200-day moving average and the $70K threshold on Friday Nov 13, touching $67,555 (its lowest since Aug 19) as $1.64B in leveraged positions were liquidated overnight, nearly 90% of them longs. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw ~$1.44B of net outflows over the prior five sessions and stablecoin supply contracted $14.2B in 30 days (fastest since June 2022); Ethereum slid to three-month lows near $1,925, extending a 14.3% seven-day loss, with the Nvidia leadership shock and Middle East tensions cited as compounding factors.
items.actionable: A $1.6B+ deleveraging cascade over the weekend is a hard risk-off signal that is moving in lockstep with the Nvidia-driven equity selloff and the Fed's hawkish repricing -- treat it as confirmation that the large cash pile should stay defensive rather than as an isolated crypto-specific event, and watch for similar forced-selling dynamics spilling into the levered silver/miners book into the Monday Asia open.

items.headline: US October PPI: headline misses at +0.3% (vs +0.4% forecast), core in line at +0.3%, but y/y hits 6.5% -- highest since 2022
items.summary: October PPI rose 0.3% m/m, below the 0.4% consensus, while core PPI matched the 0.3% forecast; on a year-over-year basis headline PPI accelerated to 6.5%, the fastest pace since November 2022. Equity futures and bonds initially rallied on the monthly miss, but Chicago Fed President Goolsbee called the broader inflation backdrop 'borderline disturbing,' and markets are now fully pricing a 25bp Fed hike (with a smaller chance of 50bp) at the Dec 8-9 FOMC rather than any near-term cut.
items.actionable: A Fed that is now debating how much to hike in December (not whether to cut) is a real-rates and dollar headwind for non-yielding gold/silver and raises the discount-rate drag on SGX REITs/banks -- the Dec 8-9 FOMC remains the key date to de-risk the levered silver position and REIT/bank sleeve into.

items.headline: Hang Seng tumbles 1.55% (HSTech -3.0%) as Nvidia leadership turmoil hits China tech; Tencent -3.1%, Xiaomi -3.7%
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index closed down 1.55% at 23,637.60 on Friday, with the Hang Seng Tech sub-index sliding 3.02% to 3,813.19, as Nvidia's leadership crisis revived concerns about tighter US export restrictions on advanced chips flowing to Chinese AI developers. Tencent fell 3.06% to HK$398.80-area levels, Xiaomi dropped 3.74%, and Alibaba fell 3.47%, while PetroChina was a rare gainer (+2.79%).
items.actionable: This is a direct, same-week mark-to-market hit on the Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC sleeve tied explicitly to the Nvidia-chip-export overhang rather than idiosyncratic company news -- expect continued correlation to US chip-policy headlines into Monday's HKEX reopen rather than a name-specific bounce.

items.headline: Gold holds near $3,890-3,915 despite tame PPI and hike bets; silver pulls back ~2% to ~$49 as COMEX inventories keep draining
items.summary: Spot gold traded around $3,890-3,915/oz on Friday, roughly steady-to-up on the day even as the tame PPI failed to dent December hike expectations, while silver fell about 1.9% to ~$49.05/oz. Global silver-backed ETP holdings are down 55M oz year-to-date to ~1.25B oz (a reversal from 2025's 278M-oz inflow year), yet COMEX registered silver inventory has reportedly fallen from ~550M oz to ~360M oz, keeping the paper-to-physical delivery-squeeze risk alive even as broad ETP flows turn net negative.
items.actionable: Gold's resilience into a hawkish Fed repricing is a constructive signal for the metals book, but silver's pullback plus draining COMEX registered stock is a two-sided setup -- the levered silver position (SLV/SI=F) faces near-term momentum risk from the hike repricing but structural upside risk if the COMEX delivery-squeeze dynamic reasserts itself.

items.headline: Silver miners Q3: Pan American and Hecla beat on record cash flow; Coeur misses despite 77% revenue growth
items.summary: Pan American Silver reported Q3 EPS of $0.69 (vs $0.66 est.) on $1.01B revenue, with net earnings more than doubling y/y to $357M. Hecla Mining beat with EPS of $0.22 (vs $0.153 est.) on record free cash flow of $151.2M (nearly tripling y/y) and a debt-free balance sheet, while Coeur Mining missed, reporting EPS of $0.11 (vs $0.19 est.) despite a 77.4% y/y revenue jump to $983.6M, with shares falling on the miss.
items.actionable: Underlying miner fundamentals (cash flow, margins) are strengthening even as spot silver pulls back on the Fed repricing -- PAAS and HL are showing genuine operating improvement that should outlast the current metals-price drawdown, while Coeur's miss is a company-specific execution flag worth isolating from the broader silver-miner thesis.

items.headline: China extends rare-earth export-control suspension to January 10, 2027; dysprosium/terbium/yttrium curbs stay in force
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce extended by two months (to Jan 10, 2027) the pause on the broad rare-earth/battery export controls that had been due to lapse in November, part of the wider trade-truce framework with Washington ahead of the Nov 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen. Licensing requirements on dysprosium, terbium and yttrium were explicitly left intact, and dysprosium oxide prices outside China have reportedly surged 242% to around $4,100/kg this year despite the broader pause.
items.actionable: The extension removes the near-term tail risk of a sudden re-imposition of the widest export controls, but the fact that heavy rare-earth curbs (dysprosium/terbium/yttrium) remain untouched keeps a structural price floor under MP/Lynas magnet-supply-chain names -- the Jan 10, 2027 date and the outcome of the Nov 18-19 Trump-Xi Shenzhen meeting are the next catalysts to watch.

items.headline: MP Materials: Q3 revenue +176% y/y to $147.7M on GM magnet-qualification ramp; insiders buy $3.35M of stock
items.summary: MP Materials posted a Nov 5 Q3 beat with revenue up 176% y/y to $147.7M and adjusted EPS swinging to +$0.04 from a $0.10 loss a year earlier, driven by higher NdPr sales volumes and pricing plus completion of General Motors magnet qualification. At the Nov 11 Baird Global Industrial Conference, management pointed to humanoid robotics, defense and advanced manufacturing as long-term magnet-demand drivers, and three insiders bought a combined $3.35M of shares this week.
items.actionable: The GM qualification and revenue ramp are company-specific fundamental positives independent of the China export-control headline cycle, and insider buying this week is a corroborating signal -- this is the cleanest standalone long idea in the rare-earths sleeve right now.

items.headline: Singapore's STI falls nearly 1% to 5,231.84, tracking regional losses on Nvidia-driven risk aversion
items.summary: The Straits Times Index closed down 50.86 points (-0.96%) at 5,231.84 on Friday, within a day's range of 5,218.23-5,272.34, as Singapore equities tracked the broader regional selloff tied to Nvidia's leadership crisis. Genting Singapore fell nearly 6% and TrickleStar dropped almost 9% on a legal demand letter, while First Resources bucked the trend, closing over 6% higher.
items.actionable: The STI's decline is being driven by imported, US-tech-headline risk aversion rather than local SGX fundamentals -- a sentiment-driven pullback is a reason to watch SGX bank/REIT names for entry points if the selloff doesn't broaden into local credit or rate concerns.

items.headline: Keppel REIT to acquire 51% of Keppel South Central; 9M 2026 net property income up 12.7%
items.summary: Keppel REIT announced at its Nov 12 Investor Day in Kuala Lumpur a proposed acquisition of a 51% interest in Keppel South Central, a newly completed 33-storey Grade-A office tower in Tanjong Pagar. For the nine months ended Sep 30, 2026, the REIT reported net property income of S$181.8M, up 12.7% year-on-year.
items.actionable: An accretive, income-generating acquisition plus double-digit NPI growth is a fundamental positive for the Keppel REIT leg of the SGX book, offsetting some of the discount-rate pressure from this week's hawkish Fed repricing -- worth tracking the acquisition's funding structure (debt vs equity) for dilution risk.

items.headline: Singapore bank Q3 split confirmed: OCBC beats and raises 2026 guidance; DBS misses on weak trading income
items.summary: OCBC's Q3 net profit rose 3% y/y to S$2.04B, beating estimates, and management raised 2026 loan-growth guidance to low double digits from high-single/low-double digits previously. DBS's net profit fell 4.8% y/y to S$2.81B, missing the S$2.90B consensus, with both DBS and UOB weighed down by weaker trading income.
items.actionable: OCBC's guidance raise supports the relative-strength case for that name within the SGX bank sleeve, while DBS's miss and trading-income weakness -- now compounding with this week's hawkish Fed repricing -- argues for keeping DBS exposure smaller than OCBC into year-end.

items.headline: Israel-Iran strike risk rises again: Netanyahu-military friction over options, Hormuz tanker incidents, drones downed near Bahrain
items.summary: Israel's security cabinet reportedly convened to weigh renewed military options against Iran amid friction between PM Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir over the scope of possible action, while Iran reported explosions on two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and the US shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones headed toward Bahrain on Nov 13. Iran separately warned that any renewed US strikes could trigger retaliation against American bases as far as Europe.
items.actionable: A live, escalating Israel-Iran flashpoint is a geopolitical tailwind for gold/silver as a hedge and keeps a shipping-risk premium under oil, while also being cited as one factor behind this weekend's broader risk-off across crypto and HK tech -- a genuine escalation (vs. posturing) would likely be the next leg up for the precious-metals book.

items.headline: Oil heads for second straight weekly decline (Brent ~$95.5-96.4, WTI ~$88.3-89.2) as US Iran blockade eases immediate supply fears
items.summary: Brent crude was on track for roughly a 2.3% weekly decline (after a 16% drop the prior week) to around $95.5-96.4/bbl, and WTI for a similar ~2.4% weekly decline to ~$88.3-89.2/bbl, as a continued US blockade of Iran eased fears of renewed regional fighting even though shipping-attack risk in the Strait of Hormuz remains elevated. Rising US crude and fuel inventories, reflecting softer refined-products demand, were also cited as a bearish driver.
items.actionable: Softer oil on weak demand is a mild positive for the inflation/Fed-hike narrative that's pressuring the metals and REIT book, but the still-live Hormuz shipping risk (see Middle East item above) means the energy complex could reverse sharply and without warning over the Sunday evening futures reopen.

items.headline: Commerce Secretary Lutnick agrees to testify over Nvidia chip-export oversight tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed
items.summary: Lutnick agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee (hearings set for Dec 3 and Dec 10, alongside ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang) after it emerged the Commerce Department knew for two years about a Bureau of Industry and Security probe into Megaspeed -- a Singapore-based buyer of over $4.8B of Nvidia's high-end AI chips -- without placing it on the export-restricted list; the probe, now with the DOJ, concerns whether those chips were diverted to China, and a Megaspeed executive is suspected by US intelligence of ties to Chinese intelligence.
items.actionable: A Singapore-incorporated entity now sits at the center of the US chip-export enforcement failure story, adding idiosyncratic headline risk around the Singapore-exposure complex and keeping the chip-export-control overhang on Chinese tech alive through the Dec 3/10 hearings -- a reason to expect recurring, hard-to-predict headline volatility in 0981.HK/0700.HK/1810.HK into December.
